name: Oracle VM VirtualBox
summary: A hosted hypervisor that manages virtual machines through a control API and runs guest CPUs, memory, devices, and I/O through a multi-context virtual machine monitor.

features.name: Hosted VM control plane
features.description: VirtualBox exposes machine and console management objects through its Main API while the VM execution process and VMM perform guest execution and lifecycle work.
benefits: Separates management clients from guest execution
Supports automation and persistent VM configuration
costs: API, saved state, and running VM state must remain coordinated
Management operations can be constrained by VM lifecycle state

features.name: Hardware-assisted VMM execution
features.description: VirtualBox separates management from guest execution, coordinates virtual CPU threads for lifecycle changes, and implements an x86 hardware-assisted virtualization manager using Intel VT-x and AMD-V.
benefits: Combines host integration with guest CPU execution
Uses hardware virtualization capabilities on supported x86 hosts
costs: Correctness depends on host CPU, kernel, and platform backends

features.name: Composable virtual device model
features.description: A VirtualBox VM combines virtual CPU and memory state with storage, networking, display, input, and guest integration devices configured through the machine and VMM layers.
benefits: Allows machine hardware and I/O topology to be configured per VM
costs: Device compatibility and configuration increase the validation surface
Guest additions and host devices create additional integration contracts

mathematical_views.question: How do API requests transition a configured VM through powered-off, running, paused, saved, and restored states?
assumptions: The Main API is the management authority
Each lifecycle operation has state preconditions
The model abstracts host process and guest OS failures

mathematical_views.question: How do guest CPU and memory state connect to virtual devices, host backends, and the VMM execution context?
assumptions: Machine components and host backends are graph nodes
Edges represent configuration or execution ownership
The model does not imply that all configurations are valid or performant
